title: A hung git push stalls the run for as long as the network lets it
description:
nu9 try 3 was ready to dispatch at 14:59:01 and did not start until 15:15:02. The feed shows the whole gap in one line:

    14:59:01  nu9  tier_derived
    15:14:47   -   remote_retried | git push failed transiently (attempt 1 of 4); waiting 2s and trying again: git push --force-wit...
    15:14:58  nu9  published
    15:15:02  nu9  dispatched

The retry policy is sound: four attempts, 2s backoff. The problem is that the FIRST push took about 15 minutes to fail before the retry logic ever ran. The backoff is carefully tuned around an operation that has no timeout of its own, so the policy's numbers describe almost none of the real delay.

A run holds still for as long as a push hangs, and the only trace is one line that reads like a minor transient. An operator watching the feed sees a 16-minute silence and one word, 'transiently', that actively misdescribes it.

The fix is a bound on the git operation itself, not a change to the retry policy: every remote git call the reconciler makes should carry a context deadline, and exceeding it should be its own feed line naming the operation and the bound - the way gate_running and wall_clock_fired already do for the two other things that can take a long time.

Check whether ls-remote and fetch share the exposure; the reconciler makes those on the same paths.

Found by watching a live run, 2026-09-20. Related to psp (a bound that does not bound) though a different mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: A remote git call that hangs is abandoned at a stated deadline and says so in the feed by name, proven by a test with a remote that never answers
